name: files
title: Workspace files (reliable reads and writes, Markdown repairs)
description: Reads and writes the files of an agent's workspace - the folder mounted at /work - so that a small local model gets them right: read_file (in parts, with the file's sha256), list_dir, glob, search, stat, diff, checksum; write_file (atomic, an existing file replaced only with the sha256 it was read with or overwrite=true, permissions, line breaks and byte order mark kept, binary-looking content refused), write_markdown (repairs what local models get wrong - a ```markdown fence around everything, literal \n, a JSON string, CRLF, trailing spaces, #Heading, an open code fence, a repeated first heading - and lists each repair; dry_run), edit_file (one exact match, or a single whitespace-tolerant one, said so), insert_lines, delete_lines, append_file, apply_patch (strict hunks, the file's text shown when one does not apply), move, copy, mkdir, delete (into /work/.trash). Every write answers lines added and removed and the new sha256. Nothing outside the mounted folders: no '..', no link followed out of a folder (the write tools follow none), no devices, pipes or sockets. Folders mounted at /ref1-/ref3 are only read. FILES_READONLY=1 refuses every write. No network.

env.name: FILES_READONLY
env.description: 1: every write tool refuses (the server only reads)

env.name: FILES_MAX_BYTES
env.description: Bytes one call reads or writes, 1K to 256M (like 8M; default 8M)

env.name: FILES_TRASH
env.description: 0: delete removes for good instead of moving into /work/.trash (default 1)

mounts.description: The workspace, writable (--mount /work=PROJECT:rw; :ro makes it read-only): the only folder written
Another folder to read from, read-only (--mount /ref1=DIR:ro); never written
Another folder to read from, read-only (--mount /ref2=DIR:ro); never written
Another folder to read from, read-only (--mount /ref3=DIR:ro); never written

notes: Made for agents on small local models (OpenCode, Codex, Hermes with --llm) that get file writes wrong: whole-file writes need the sha256 read_file gave (no blind clobbering), edits need one exact match, and write_markdown repairs and reports. The workspace may be the very project folder the agent works in (sandbox-ai refuses a folder inside a tree a sandbox can write, not that folder itself); one entry per project (sandbox-ai mcp add files --as files-NAME). Writes are atomic (temporary file, fsync, rename) and never through a link; .git and .trash are not written. Recommended: allow the read tools, ask for delete and move, or give FILES_READONLY=1 where the agent should only read.
